items.quote: We clearly believe that 14%-15% is definitely the guidance that we've given on the basis of best estimate at that point of time.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue growth delivered at 17% versus 14%-15% guidance
items.quote: But we delivered 17% in the last quarter And we very clearly see opportunity because for us both B2C and B2B engines are firing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 27%-28% from current 24.4% driven by mix, productivity, and network utilization
items.quote: If you see what are the key ambition, if you see the ambition is to improve our EBITDA margin from 24.4% to 27% to 28% and what are the key drivers for it?

items.statement: Radiology mini-hubs capex of INR35-40 lakhs per center, planning 50 centers in year 1 and 50 more in year 2
items.quote: So, roughly about INR35 lakhs-INR40 lakhs per investment would be good enough for us to run a good mini, you know, hubs, you know, to start with.

items.statement: Adding 250-300 collection centers per quarter, plan to accelerate with 800-1,000 own centers to become more productive
items.quote: There is a regular addition of 250 to 300 centers every quarter. We have a plan to further accelerate this, as I mentioned some time back.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics acquisition turned from loss-making to high single-digit EBITDA in year 1, targeting company-level EBITDA by year 3
items.quote: 1 year after acquisition, t his is high single -digit EBITDA and we are now , I was guiding everyone that, maybe year 3 we will be close to the company levels of EBITDA

items.statement: Acquisition strategy focuses on clean businesses with credibility, targeting geographies with low presence and skill gaps; 25 past acquisitions with successful integration playbook
items.quote: We only acquire places where the, the brand that we are acquiring, the lab that we are acquiring, has got good credibility in the market.

items.statement: International business operates 24 labs in 5 countries, self-funded with no capital from India, leading in Kenya and Zambia, top 3 in Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania
items.quote: There is no capital that's been flowing from the Indian operations to international operation to build business there. You know, they are generating their own money.

items.statement: Target to reduce working capital from double-digit to single-digit days through automation of receivables and supply chain
items.quote: Our aspiration is to take our working capital to a single digit from currently the double-digit working capital.

items.statement: Specialty and semi-specialty tests have uniform pricing across India, routine tests vary by market; Tier 3 unit economics equal or better than metros due to lower costs
items.quote: Our semi-special tests and our specialized tests actually have a similar price point across India. So whether you pick up from a small market like Sangli or you pick up from Bombay, for the specialized test, the price is the same.

items.statement: Broad-based growth across all four regions, Tier 1/2/3, B2C and B2B both firing, specialty and TruHealth driving growth
items.quote: All the four regions are doing well for us, and the Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, all the, you know, geographies are doing well for us. So, largely a broad-based growth that we are seeing.

items.statement: B2C-B2B revenue mix currently 60-40, B2C growing faster driven by digital, home collection, and network expansion in Tier 2/3
items.quote: Yes, currently it is 60-40, 59-41 to be precise. The center acceleration will really go, in faster than what we are currently doing. That's one great opportunity for B2C as to get better.

items.statement: Home collection services cover 2,200 PIN codes, contributing ~25% of revenue and growing 40%+ per quarter
items.quote: I think home collection, we today service around 2,200 PIN codes across the country where we provide home collection services and I think till couple of years back, it was really a marginal sort of business did not make sense at all at that time, now contributing 25%-odd and that is really growing almost 40% plus on every quarter.

items.statement: Market share stable in key cities (Mumbai, Chennai, Pune) despite competition from health tech, pharma, and other players
items.quote: Our share of the market in the key towns, like, let's say Mumbai or Chennai or Pune remain intact. In fact, we start doing better in these towns.

items.statement: No benefit from CGHS price increases as CGHS business negligible; competitors' CGHS benefit fading from Q3 FY27
items.quote: We didn't have any benefit of the CGHS price increase because our CGHS business was very low and almost negligible, you know, earlier. But some of the other operators have got huge benefit which anyway will start fading away from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Disciplined M&A approach avoiding businesses with governance issues; will not overpay for acquisitions lacking synergy value in pathology
items.quote: We are being disciplined about it. We do see opportunities there, but I think the kind of opportunities we think are more likely are businesses which have been built in the last 10 years with people thinking we can scale it and they have realized that this is now not so easy.

items.statement: Management KPIs structured in three buckets: current year AOP/stock value, long-term strategic projects with milestones, and annual focus area (e.g., controls, culture)
items.quote: One obviously is, look, there is importance of the presence here and now as well. So obviously, a direct linkage to not only AOP but also the stock value that we are able to generate for shareholders, right?

items.statement: Beyond diagnostics strategy exploring allied healthcare services (asset-light) to become health partner; no clear blueprint yet, evaluating 3-4 ideas for IRR and right to win
items.quote: The idea is to build a business out of it and a serious business which we can win in. Now how big that business can be, what margins it can be, we will have to come back.

items.statement: Advanced radiology (MRI/CT) not a core strategy; may pilot 1-2 centers in preventive health but limited to 8-10 centers long-term due to ROIC and governance concerns
items.quote: Just on the MRI/CT front, I do not think we will be looking at that area at this point. What Suren, of course, was referring to is the mini hubs, the basic radiology.

items.statement: Building in-house tech team to reduce vendor dependence; using AI to cut call tickets by 50% and accelerate development cycles
items.quote: We are using AI in order to reduce the number of call tickets that we have, right? So we are also ensuring that the TAT at which if some customer calls, how can we resolve that issue in less time, in 50% of the time.

items.statement: Commitment to maintain regular dividend payouts while improving ROCE through disciplined capital allocation and asset-light growth
items.quote: We would like to maintain regular dividend payouts.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to northwards of 60% YoY from initial 30-40%
items.quote: We believe the order book is streaming up well, and there is a potential in northwards of 60% for the current year now.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 35-40% for FY27
items.quote: It is not the guidance, we've always guided between 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Targeting INR1,000 crores top line by FY29
items.quote: We are fully capitalized to achieve our turnover of a top line of INR1,000 crores, which is in the near future.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,300+ crores across dredging, charter & hire, and shipbuilding
items.quote: Our detailed order book schedule reflects a balance order book of more than INR1,300 crores, comprising approximately INR240 crores towards dredging, INR850 crores towards charter and hire and INR240 crores in shipbuilding.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR3,500+ crores across three segments
items.quote: Looking beyond the existing order book, our current bid pipeline is approximately INR3,500-plus crores, dredging stands at INR1,200-plus crores, charter and hire stands at INR1,100-plus crores and shipbuilding stands at INR1,400-plus crores.

items.statement: Capex of close to INR1,000 crores planned over next 1.5 years across dredging, chartering and shipbuilding
items.quote: So currently, we are undergoing a capex of close to INR1,000 crores, which will be between now and within the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Capex breakdown: INR450 crores for dredging, INR250 crores for Green Tugs, balance for shipyard
items.value: INR450 crores dredging, INR250 crores Green Tugs
items.quote: So approximately INR250 crores is going into the construction of Green Tugs and green vessels, close to INR450 crores will be in the dredging business and the balance will be in the creation of the shipyard and the shipbuilding business.

items.statement: Saphale shipyard Phase 1 expected operational by end of FY27, full capacity 18 vessels per annum
items.quote: Before the end of the current financial year, we believe we will start launching vessels from the yard. And once in full capacity, the yard will be able to deliver 14 vessels under Phase I. And by the time it completes all the phases, it will reach to 18 vessels.

items.statement: Expect dredging volumes to scale with larger capacity dredgers enabling higher value contracts
items.quote: Our strategy is to complement our existing diversified fleet with larger capacity dredgers, which will allow us to undertake significantly higher volumes and participate in larger value and more technically demanding contracts.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 64%, PAT margin 54% but guided margins 35-40% EBITDA, 25-30% PAT
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR73.41 crores, increasing 258% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of approx. 64%. Profit after tax stands at INR62.75 crores, representing growth of 466% year-on-year basis with a PAT margin of approximately 54%.

items.statement: Dredging margins expected to expand with volume growth; shipbuilding margins post-subsidy exceed 35%
items.quote: Post subsidy, they will easily go beyond 35%.

items.statement: Revenue mix shift targeted: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering 5% in 2-3 years
items.quote: 2 to 3 years from now, we believe that dredging will contribute between 45% to 50% of the revenue mix. Shipbuilding will be between 40% to 45%, and the chartering business will be at 5%.

items.statement: Shipbuilding order book from IWAI; targeting state governments, maritime boards for green ferries
items.quote: So presently, the current order book is from Inland Waterways Authority of India. We want to further build order book in terms of green ferries from various different authorities, which will also contribute towards the water metro system.

items.statement: Low competition in dredging; selective bidding maintains margins; room for new players but high entry barriers
items.quote: Dredging, it's very little to no competition, and we've been easily improving our efficiency by sweating our assets better. So thus far, we believe that competition has not played a huge role in lowering our margins.

items.statement: Preparing for Samudra Manthan deep-sea mining initiative with larger dredgers (5,000-7,000 cu m); meaningful deployment in 2-3 years
items.quote: we are preparing ourselves for that kind of execution going forwar d, wherein we are buying larger dredgers now with the capacity of more than 5,000 and 7,000 cubic meters, which can be used for such scheme

items.statement: No additional loans needed for shipbuilding working capital; stage payments fund execution; interest subvention up to 3% available for Green Tug loans
items.quote: So our cash flow that we generate from these sales payments supports the working structure that we have, and we don't need to take loans or any kind of support for execution of these works.

items.statement: Subcontracting charges reduced to 5-6% of turnover from FY26 onwards as JV contracts ended
items.quote: In year FY26, you will see a subcontracting charges of not more than 5% to 6% of our turnover.

items.statement: Historical bid hit rate exceeds 50% over last 11 years
items.quote: So in the past, we've always had in the last 11 years, a hit rate in excess of 50%. That's been the history.

items.statement: Dredging business considered perpetual; government ports not planned for full privatization in coming decade
items.quote: Not all the government ports in the short term or in the long term have been planned for complete privatization. We have been working for majorly the government entities over the last 11 years. And navigation will always remain the part or the responsibility of Government of India.

items.statement: Exploring export opportunities from European market for 3,000 DWT vessels; awaiting comfortable payment terms
items.quote: So yes, there are possibilities of export orders, which we are kind of exploring from the European market, wherein vessels to the DWT capacity of 3,000-odd tonnes, which the owners are looking to build through the designers in India.

items.statement: Green Tug contracts with major government ports (Visakhapatnam, V.O. Chidambaranar) have 15-year fixed charter with take-or-pay guarantee
items.quote: The Green Tug contracts are with Government of India, the 2 major ports, Port of Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar Port. They have a perpetual requirement for the tug. So as long as whether they use the tug or they don't use the tug, there is a fixed charter under the contract that we will continue to get for a period of 15 years.

items.statement: DCI Mangrol project dues of INR16 crores fully received
items.quote: So, we have received all the funds now.

items.quote: Mr. Nautiyal has not been keeping good health since mid-July and for a few days, he worked from home. Thereafter, he was on leave till yesterday and due to continued health concerns, he decided to tender in his early retirement request to the NRC.

items.statement: Carol Furtado appointed as Interim MD and CEO subject to RBI approval; she has over three decades of experience and is a key member of the leadership team.
items.quote: The Board has requested Ms. Carol Furtado, the Executive Director, to take over as Interim MD and CEO, subject to RBI approval. Ms. Carol is a seasoned banker with over 3 decades of extensive experience across business, strategy, operations, people and institutional functions.

items.statement: NRC mandated to search for a permanent successor; search process started immediately and expected to submit names to RBI in 3 to 4 months.
items.quote: We are starting the search process. In the normal course, we wanted to start somewhere around October, November. But because of this Mr. Nautiyal's early retirement, we are starting the search process quickly. We are hopeful that in about 3 to 4 months' time, we should be able to complete this process.

items.statement: Internal candidates will be considered for MD role; Carol Furtado has expressed desire to be a candidate for the regular MD position.
items.quote: We will definitely consider internal candidates. I'm sure Carol is very serious candidate now. She has also expressed her desire to be a candidate for a regular position as MD.

items.statement: Vikas Agarwal joined as Business Head, MSME; he is a Chartered Accountant with over 25 years of experience across MSME, business banking, retail banking, credit, product development and distribution.
items.quote: Today, we are happy to announce the joining of Mr. Vikas Agarwal as Business Head, MSME. Vikas is a Chartered Accountant and a seasoned banker with over 25 years of experience across MSME, business banking, retail banking, credit, product development and distribution.

items.statement: Management reiterated commitment to meet FY27 guidance; no change to strategy previously outlined and communicated.
items.quote: We remain on track to meet our FY27 guidance. The Ujjivan team is committed to delivering strong performance in FY27 and beyond with no change to the strategy previously outlined and communicated.

items.statement: Capital raise delay will not impact FY27 growth momentum; bank is well capitalized and committed to growth plans for FY27.
items.quote: We remain on track to meet our FY27 guidance, and we are committed to delivering a strong performance. We remain well capitalized and committed to our growth plans for FY27.

items.statement: Q1 loan book grew approximately 29% year-on-year; GNPA at 2.2%; secured book share grew past 50% as diversification strategy progresses.
items.quote: Q1 loan book growth of approximately 29% year -on-year with GNPA at 2.2% is testament to our continued execution. Our strategic priority of diversifying the loan book has re sulted in the secured book share growing past 50%.

items.statement: Festive season looks promising backed by capacity additions and robust domestic economic performance; brand campaign poised for launch during festive season.
items.quote: As we look ahead, the festive season looks promising, backed by our capacity additions supported by robust domestic economic performance. This will be further augmented by the brand campaign poised for launch during the festive season.

items.statement: CASA book grew at a healthy 38% year-on-year; overall cost of funds at 6.9% for Q1 despite market pressure on deposits.
items.quote: Even though the market has been under a lot of pressure on the deposits front, the bank has been able to grow the CASA book at a healthy 38% year -on-year with overall cost of funds at 6.9% for Q1.

items.statement: People strategy emphasizes mix of internal talent and acquiring right talent from market as cornerstone of consistent performance.
items.quote: People strategy is a large part of Ujjivan. The mix of internal and acquiring the right talent from the market has been the cornerstone of our consistent performance.

items.statement: Board confirmed no material factor apart from health for Nautiyal's sudden exit; no issue with business strategies or working of the bank.
items.quote: No, absolutely, no. Absolutely no. I think it is his personal call. But absolutely, there is no issue with regard to the business strategies or the working of the bank. I can assure you on that.

items.statement: Board acknowledged need for more robust succession planning in future to avoid leadership instability.
items.quote: So we did not feel the urgency at that point of time, but we will definitely keep it in mind in future to really have a more robust succession planning in such eventualities.

items.statement: Diversification strategy well on trajectory; strategic diversification progressing as planned.
items.quote: Also, just to state, our strategic diversification is also well on its trajectory.

items.statement: Management declined to comment on timeline for transition to universal bank; focused on meeting laid down goals and diversification strategy.
items.quote: We would not like to comment on that. We are quite focused on meeting the goals that we have already laid down and our diversification strategy is, again, as I say, well on its trajectory. Yes, we are proceeding towards that.

items.statement: Demand momentum from end of FY26 carried into Q1 FY27 with double-digit revenue and volume growth across all product categories.
items.quote: Now the demand momentum that we described at the close of FY26 has carried through into the first quarter of FY27. Revenue has grown in double digits, the first such quarter in almost two years for us. And while the price increases that we implemented also aided in achieving this outcome, what is more encouraging is that volumes also grew in double digits and did so across the product portfolio.

And I'm not saying they are bad, or we are good, or we are bad, and we are good. It's just that there's no DNA match, so we do not like to do that.

items.statement: Health insurance combined operating ratio at 93%; ₹30 capital generates ₹12 return (40% ROE); reinsurance at 20% could yield 60% ROE on 50% ceded.
items.quote: We are operating at a combined operating ratio in health of 93%. Please appreciate, for ₹ 30 of capital , with ₹5 of interest income on that and ₹7, that is ₹ 12 on ₹ 30, that's 40% return on equity. If you reinsure that, you can today reinsure commodity at 20%. And let's say you reinsure 50% of that, then on your 50%, you can make 60% return on equity.

items.statement: No knee-jerk decisions or mass layoffs; company run for long-term growth; hiring slowdown expected but existing hires to mature into higher productivity.
items.quote: I just want to be very clear that we are going to make no knee -jerk decisions, there will be no mass layoffs of any kind, we run the company for long-term growth, and we will calibrate that growth to the new reality, but at no point are we going to make decisions which will hurt our colleagues in any sort of unfair way.

items.statement: Marketing spend at margin was ₹100 to make ₹100; under new economics, spending ₹100 to make ₹30 is unviable; marketing and operational hiring to be cut until settlement.
items.quote: Now, at the margins, when we were spending money on Google, and using these efforts to sell, we were barely at 100% right now. Like, we were spending ₹100 to make ₹100, at the margin. So clearly, that part will become unviable for us. If suddenly, instead of ₹100, I'm making ₹30, I can't spend 100 rupees to make 30 rupees. I obviously cannot.

items.statement: Industry-wide impact on all distributors and insurers; collaboration needed to determine next steps; no single competitor stands with Policybazaar today indicating industry difficulty.
items.quote: This is not something which is just for Policybazaar. This is a very industry-wide proposal which has been taken out, impacting all the distributors, and even insurance companies, and the way the insurance distribution mode l has worked in India so far. I think everyone from the industry has to collaborate and figure out what is the right next step for this, including us, obviously.

items.statement: Exploring manufacturing (insurance/reinsurance) to defend against unfair economics; higher probability of own manufacturing capability if quality not rewarded and benefits not passed to customers.
items.quote: So, I think now, if I was to think about it, if I was to give a probability, I would say, yes, there would be a higher probability of us having some manufacturing capability of our own, because we have to defen d ourselves in that situation, where our f inancials are impacted, but the benefit is not passed on to the customer, and thus we are not allowed to win.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of minimum 20% YoY for FY27 and PAT growth of 25-30% YoY
items.quote: As I told you, we'll be growing at about 20% minimum year-on-year. And bottom line will grow at minimum at 25% to 30%. PAT will keep on going up by about 25% to 30%, top line will grow up by 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 24-25% for FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin will be maintained at about 24% to 25%.

items.statement: INR30 crores capex planned for FY27 from IPO proceeds to add capacity
items.quote: We have got INR30 crores of object now. We will be implementing that.

items.statement: INR30 crores capex to add INR100 crores revenue capacity within one year
items.quote: We have got INR30 crores allotted for capex this year, and we'll be implementing that within a period of one year.

items.statement: Current capacity 35 lakh fittings/month, targeting 70 lakh/month in 3 years
items.quote: Today, we are manufacturing around 35 lakhs of fittings every month, and the proceeds that we have got now from IPO, we are going to go to 70 lakhs per month.

items.statement: Current plant utilization 60-70%, maintaining 20-25% extra capacity for new customers
items.quote: Currently, we are utilizing -- I'll tell you, we are utilizing it about 60% -70%. And we always keep extra capacity, the reason is that when new OE comes with about 10 crores, 15 crores order, he asks us, 'Do you have a capacity?' So, we have to show the capacity to him.

items.statement: 6.5 acres land approved for new plant, targeting 2x productivity, ready in 2 years
items.quote: We are going in for 6.5 acres of land. It has been approved in the board now, and we will be taking this land within a period of next 3 months to 4 months' time. And then since it's a long time to get the approvals from the government, and then building and construction will take about a year, so we'll have to be ready within two years, this plant will be ready.

items.statement: Forging capacity expanding with two mechanical presses at Shirwal and Nashik
items.quote: Now, two mechanical presses. One mechanical press has already landed in our plant in Shirwal, and one more capacity of mechanical press is landing at our Nashik plant, so we are increasing.

items.statement: No traditional order book; annual schedules from OEMs with 70-80% OEM revenue share
items.quote: Order book is more or less, more or less, we have got schedules for annual schedules from all OEMs. So, we don't have an order book. They give us a contract order with price, and they keep on sending us schedules.

items.statement: Domestic growth expected 15-20% vs industry 7-8% due to share gains and new OEMs
items.quote: Even domestic business also I'm expecting a growth of about 15% to 20%. Although the business in India is growing at about 7%, 8%, we will grow at 20%, because we will be getting more SOBs, share of business, from the existing customers, as well as we'll add few more OEMs.

items.statement: New OEM wins include Tata Hitachi, Sany, Fluidconnecto from bauma exhibition
items.quote: New OEMs which are now we got in bauma are Tata Hitachi, it's a major OEM, and then Sany, a Chinese manufacturer, and then there was one more, is Fluidconnecto.

items.statement: Export at 30% of revenue (25% USA, 7-8% Europe), targeting 50% export in 5 years
items.quote: We have already prepared a plan for five years, and in five years, we have decided to go for 50% export and 50% domestic. That is the plan. Today, we are at about 30% export.

items.statement: US subsidiary being formed to serve John Deere's 47 US plants, 6-7 plants already approved
items.quote: We have been approved in all their plants, and business from about 6 plants to 7 plants have already started coming to us. They are insisting us to supply all the fittings from USA. So, we are therefore opening a company in USA, and that is also being sanctioned in the board today.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 19.6% vs 21.5% YoY due to raw material cost lag; price revisions effective Q2
items.quote: EBITDA margin, which is 19.6% for the current year or the current quarter compared to 21.5% for the previous year of the same quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve 0.5-1% annually to reach 25% in 2-3 years via export mix and Kaizen
items.quote: Year-on-year, it will go up by 1%. There are two reasons for it, because as I told you, we'll be increasing the export that will give us a better price. And second point is that we have implemented all Kaizen activities, so our operational efficiencies will keep on going

items.statement: 80% standard fittings, 20% custom; developing stainless steel for data centers/oil & gas
items.quote: Last two years, we have CIN No. - L99999MH1978PLC020853 already developed the range which is required for data centers, but that is also applicable to oil and gas. Similar fittings are required in data center in stainless steel, and we have just started manufacturing these fittings, and we'll be entering into this data center opportunity over a period of next one year's time positively

items.statement: R&D spend at 1% of revenue; evaluating valves as higher value-added products
items.quote: R&D, we are spending around 1% of our revenue.

items.statement: 170 direct OEM customers, no single customer >15% revenue; wallet share 10-100%
items.quote: We have around 170 direct customers and more than seven active distributors, and we have got a presence across 11 countries for the export.

items.statement: Railway (IRIS), Defence (DRDO), Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock registrations done; revenue in 5-6 months
items.quote: We have got certified now with IRIS, which is a railway certification, so we are now eligible to enter into railway business. We are also registered with DRDO, that is a defence organization, so we have now chance to enter into defence as well. And we have also registered ourselves in Cochin Shipyard and Mazagon Dock.

items.statement: Domestic competitor <50% of Hy-Tech turnover; Parker 2x price, no Chinese competition
items.quote: Our next competitor is less than half our turnover. So, we are enjoying this leading position in the market.

items.statement: Price revision compensation from OEMs for raw material and other cost increases
items.quote: We requested all our OEMs for the price revision. And that price revision we got it effective 1st of April, but we will be getting it in the second quarter. So, that profit, which is now lying with OEM, they will transfer it to us, and that will come in the second quarter.

items.statement: IPO raised INR135.7 crores including INR60 crores fresh issue; proceeds for capex, debt repayment, general corporate
items.quote: Following our IPO, the as sir said, company has raised INR135.7 crores, including INR60 crores through the fresh issue. The fresh issue proceeds are being utilized towards the identified objectives, including the capital expenditure, repayment of our borrowings, and general corporate purpose.

items.statement: Market size: INR2,000 crores India, INR20,000 crores USA, INR10,000 crores Europe, INR8,000 crores others
items.quote: The total requirement of this fittings all over the world is 40,000 crores. How much? 40,000 crores. CIN No. - L99999MH1978PLC020853 Out of that, 20,000 crores fittings are consumed in USA, 10,000 crores of fittings are consumed in Europe, and around 2,000 crores are consumed in India

items.statement: Geopolitical risk: limiting US exposure to 25% of revenue, diversifying to Europe, Australia, Dubai
items.quote: We don't want to increase that. As I told you, the philosophy and policy of Hy-Tech is to spread the business all over. What happens if the Trump relationship changes? We can't afford to have too much of business from USA.

items.statement: Elder son managing US marketing; 100% US subsidiary being formed
items.quote: As you all know, my son, my elder son, is in USA, so he will be taking care of that business. He is taking care of all marketing business in USA, and because of his presence in USA, USA business is going to be our major focus for next 2 years-3 years.

items.statement: Targets 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth for FY27 on consolidated basis, with +/-5% variability
items.quote: Based on our current visibility and business outlook, we are definitely targeting 20% and 25% growth for this current fiscal year in our revenues and our EBITDA, respectively. Of course, this could be plus-minus some percentage, 5%, due to this global operating environmental uncertainties that we are all aware of today.

items.statement: Expects PAT growth lower than EBITDA due to depreciation drag; cash PAT growth upwards of 25%
items.quote: And this drag would slightly reduce the percentage growth on the PAT from the previous year. But if you look at cash PAT, which is PAT plus depreciation, then the growth is upwards of 25% as mentioned by Anil for EBITDA.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR200-250 crores per year for next 2-3 years, funded by internal accruals and partner capital
items.quote: But the visibility that I can currently give you based on our operating cash flows is minimum INR200 crores to INR250 crores each year for the next two to three years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was approximately INR68 crores
items.quote: Our capex for quarter one FY '27 is approximately INR68 crores.

items.statement: Ujjain fermentation facility has 400 kL capacity; Phase 1 expansion of 600 kL planned for Q3 FY27 start, 15-18 month build
items.quote: And the Phase 1 is this, which you're referring to, 600 KL, which we need to, of course, build as a brownfield expansion. This would need typically 15 to 18 months. But before it kicks in, we would like to utilize our existing 400 KL capacities.

items.statement: API capacity utilization at 70-80%
items.quote: It's roughly about 70%-80%, Sagar.

items.statement: Signed 5-year take-or-pay contract for insulin drug substance; 10-year take-or-pay contract with US alternate protein player; term sheet with European alternate protein player
items.quote: Just to put it on record, one, we have signed a 5 year take-or-pay contract for insulin as a drug substance in the biopharma space. And, two, in the biomanufacturing, a 10-year take-or-pay contract with a US-based company for an alternative protein product, and, three, it is a term sheet which we have signed with a European company for an alternate protein product, again.

items.statement: Filed first DCV ANDA in August 2026; second filing scheduled for Q4 FY27; term sheet with large US pharma MNC for DCV products, definitive agreement expected early Q3 FY27
items.quote: On Complex Injectable business, we are very happy to announce that we have filed the first molecule ANDA for DCV in this month, and the filing of the second molecule is scheduled for quarter four. On the licensing arrangement for these two DCV products in the U.S., the term sheet, as Anil mentioned, is already in place, and the formal agreement is in a very advanced stage, with the signing expecte

items.statement: Strong traction in biomanufacturing CDMO; existing 400 kL largely booked; visibility for 4x capacity expansion from two signed customers; advanced discussions with half a dozen potential customers each needing million-liter scale
items.quote: And this is basically just for the simplification purpose. Let me just say that I divide it into Phase 0, Phase 1, and Phase 2. This is what we have so far put into our agreements. The Phase 0 is that that my customers have to utilize our existing capacities. And because this this capacity is not enough, we have to go with the Phase 1 and eventually the Phase 2.

items.statement: API gross margins 60%+ in Q1 FY27; targets maintaining ~60% gross margin and ~30% EBITDA margin for API business
items.quote: Gross margins in the API business remains strong at 60% plus for quarter one FY '27, and API EBITDA for quarter one FY '27 stood at INR66 crores, a steady 9% year-on-year growth driven by sales volume growth and a strong gross margin mix.

items.statement: Expects biotech CDMO and complex injectables to achieve >70% gross margins and >35% EBITDA margins at maturity, in line with industry trends
items.quote: Usually, this industry trend is higher than 70% as gross margins and higher than 35% as EBITDA margins. And because we are into the same orbit where we have a very differentiated fermentation biotech CMO and very differentiated device called dual-chamber platform, right? So, we believe that we should be in the similar margin profile.

items.statement: Backward integration from sterols enables make-vs-buy flexibility protecting margins; not backward integrated on solvents
items.quote: We can always make all the intermediates that we want. We can always buy, should someone choose to supply at reasonable conditions, right? So, this make versus buy always allow us to always sort of look into our margins which are they are fairly predictable.

items.statement: API revenue shifting toward regulated markets and higher-value products, improving margins
items.quote: We have been actually consolidating our profit margins, as you have seen, because we are moving more and more towards the regulated markets and more and more towards those customers that are giving us long-term contracts for the products which are more valuable than the other ones, right?

items.statement: Serves 200+ customers across 40+ countries; 70% of FY26 revenue from customers >7 years; top 5 customer relationships >10 years
items.quote: We serve over 200 customers across more than 40 countries, including innovators, big pharma, and also world's leading generic and specialty pharma companies across North America, Europe, Latin America, and Asia.

items.statement: New business opex drag of INR23 crores/quarter and depreciation of INR11 crores/quarter to continue for next 2-3 quarters
items.value: INR23 crores opex, INR11 crores depreciation per quarter
items.quote: On the expenses drag of expenses from this new businesses, this INR23 crores as a run rate should more or less continue for the next two, three quarters in terms of the run rate of expenses, and similarly on the depreciation about INR11 crores.

items.statement: Net debt INR398 crores as of June 30; reduced to ~INR326 crores after IPO proceeds of INR142 crores and Q2 capex
items.quote: Our net debt position as on 30th June stood at INR398 crores, and with the recent IPO proceeds of INR142 crores, which is net of expenses, and considering further capex in the September quarter, our net debt as of today roughly stands around INR326 crores.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR142 crores net of expenses received
items.quote: and with the recent IPO proceeds of INR142 crores, which is net of expenses, and considering further capex in the September quarter, our net debt as of today roughly stands around INR326 crores.

items.statement: API asset turnover ~1.5x on INR650 crores invested capital generating INR900 crores revenue
items.quote: In our existing API facility, which is Rau site and the Pithampur SEZ site, we have cumulatively invested more than INR650 crores over the years, helping us generate around INR900 crores of API revenue at an asset turnover ratio of about 1.5x.

items.statement: R&D spend consistently 3-5% of sales; expects to continue at 3-4% with potential increase to 5%
items.quote: We consistently have been investing about 3% to 4% of our sales as R&D, and we expect this to continue, probably with a slight increase as well to about 5% in the future.

items.statement: Completed US FDA audit at Pithampur site in August 2026; submitted responses to procedural observations, awaiting EIR
items.quote: On the API business, we have recently completed a U.S. FDA audit at our Pithampur site in August 2026. We have submitted our responses to the few procedural observations and are awaiting the EIR.

items.statement: Premarin generic launch timing uncertain; dependent on partner's formulation development and FDA approval
items.quote: It's difficult, because we have finished our R&D part, and we are we are in no control over the formulation development. So, at this point of time, I cannot give any guidance with respect to time for our Premarin generic launch as a formulation.

items.statement: Biologics/insulin revenue expected early next fiscal year (FY28) after DCGI approval and stability studies
items.quote: So, we expect not all this to happen in the current fiscal year. Hence, the revenues from our biologics division is likely to kick in, in early next fiscal year.

items.statement: Milestone revenues from CDMO/injectables in H2 FY27 (Q3/Q4) to offset new business opex drag
items.quote: However, at the higher level, I can tell you that whatever this drag we have on the operating expenses from both our subsidiaries will be set off in the milestone revenues that we are about to have in Q3, Q4, which is H2 in total.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR218 crores (7% YoY); API revenue INR215 crores (6% YoY); consolidated EBITDA INR45 crores; net profit INR14 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for quarter one FY '27 stood at INR218 crores, representing a growth of 7% year-on-year. This revenue was largely contributed by our API business, with revenues at INR215 crores and a growth of 6% year-on-year driven largely by volume increase.

items.statement: Management declined to provide full-year revenue or profitability guidance for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We are not supposed to be giving any kind of guidance for full year. So, as the numbers will come, we will be disclosing the actual numbers every quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue and profitability numbers for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: No. We cannot give any forward -looking numbers, so that is not yet, like, company has not planned to disclose anything like that.

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,500 crores capex in FY27 funded by customer advances, IPO proceeds, and partial debt
items.quote: FY27, we are targeting to conclude around INR1,500 crores of capex, and additional INR1,500 crores, whatever has happened, I exactly don't have the numbers in front of me right now, but we will be doing additional INR1,500 crores of capex in FY27.

items.statement: Sharon AI 8,200 GPU deployment in Sydney expected to go live by early to mid Q3 FY27
items.quote: From Q3 onwards, we will see the revenue coming in from the AI factory in Sydney.

items.statement: Own GPU capacity target of 1,500 GPUs to be deployed by mid to end of Q4 FY27
items.quote: The target is to touch around 1,500 GPUs. We'll be deploying those by January or February next year, which will be mid of Q4. Mid of Q4 or end of Q4.

items.statement: International GPU pipeline exceeds 50,000 GPUs across multiple locations
items.quote: We have a strong funnel of more than 50,000 GPUs right now, and we are trying to figure out how we will deliver that, from where, all locations, which all locations we can deliver the pipeline.

items.statement: GPU supply constraints with delivery delays of 4-9 months; leveraging relationships to expedite
items.quote: It is already a constraint. There is a delivery timeline delay of 4 months, 6 months, 9 months also. So, we are leveraging our relationships to get the deliveries expedited.

items.statement: Domestic order book of INR 3,000 crores with 3-year duration; international order book much larger
items.quote: Domestic business, we have got around INR3,000 crores of an order book with us. International is much larger than that.

items.statement: Domestic order book growing at 30-40% CAGR
items.quote: Domestic, currently, we are seeing a CAGR of 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Targeting PAT margins of 15-20% on GPU leasing deals; will not accept lower margins
items.quote: We are targeting PAT margins in the range of 15% to 20%. So, that's our target PAT margin. We will not work for anything lesser than that.

items.statement: SaaS segment has highest profitability; IaaS margins improving with GPU business growth
items.quote: Our profitability is high on Software-as-a-Service. But now, with growth of AI factories, with growth of GPU business, we are seeing more numbers coming from Infrastructure-as-a-Service and better margins also coming from Infrastructure-as-a-Service.

items.statement: GPU rental rates currently $5-6 per hour for B300 GPUs; rates expected to increase 25% by January
items.quote: The industry standard where people are currently billing upwards of $5 per GPU per hour that is what everyone in the industry, $5, $6 per hour. So, we are also going to bill our customer in that range only.

items.statement: GPU prices continuously increasing for next 3-5 years due to demand-supply gap; NVIDIA unable to fulfill demand
items.quote: Continuously going up. Next three to five years, it is anticipated that the rates will go up. The demand is such that NVIDIA is not able to fulfill the demand, neither the semiconductor companies, neither NVIDIA.

items.statement: International GPU demand desperate with 12-18 month advances; Indian demand growing but slower
items.quote: There is desperation in international customers to get the GPU services. So, we are happy to provide services to them. They are good paymasters, giving 12 to 18 months of advances also.

items.statement: GPU useful life up to 8 years as older GPUs cascade from AI labs to gaming, e-commerce, video rendering
items.quote: So, we see a useful life of GPU running up to 8 years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue split: IaaS 51%, Managed Services 31.31%, SaaS 17.55%; mix expected to remain steady
items.quote: For Q1 FY27, our IaaS revenue was 51% of the total revenue, Managed Service revenue was 31.31%, and SaaS revenue was 17.55%. And this will go steady in future years as well.

items.statement: GPU revenue classified under IaaS; currently leasing GPUs from partners, minimal owned GPUs live in Q1
items.quote: GPU revenue also gets classified under Infrastructure-as-a-Service. So, the GPUs can either be owned by us or the GPUs can be leased through a partner. We will either lease it from a partner or we will buy and deploy those. At the moment, majorly we are leasing those from our partners.

items.statement: Sharon AI deal locked for 7 years; customer concentration risk mitigated by appreciating asset and advance payments
items.quote: We have locked Sharon for 7 years. Our rates are already like discovered with them. And if you read the contract that we have done with Sharon, our contract is locked for 7 years.

items.statement: NVIDIA approval required for international client offtake; rigorous process followed
items.quote: So, we actually, when we get a demand from our customers, we discuss that with our NVIDIA counterparts also. They have to approve. Once they approve, then we deploy as per their approvals.

items.statement: INR 1,177 crores customer advance received; amortized monthly over contract period
items.quote: So, again, this advance pertains to the same order , which will go live from Q3 FY '27. And advance will get amortized over a period of contract on monthly basis.

items.statement: Partial debt to fund FY27 capex alongside customer advances and IPO proceeds
items.quote: Customer advance, IPO proceed, and partial debt.

items.statement: Strategy to keep people cost low by using partner employees for AI factory projects
items.quote: We are also -- wherever we are partnering, we are telling the partners also to put their employees in the project, and the entire AI factory would come from the partner, people may also come from the partner. Plan is to keep people cost as low as possible.

items.statement: AGM postponed due to shareholder spike to 190,000 post-listing; ROC extension sought for compliance
items.quote: on 4th September, we got listed. And the list of shareholders that suddenly spiked to almost 1,90,000 shareholders. And so, all the arrangements that need to be made for them was a little bit difficult. And we also have to follow the timelines for arranging all these facilities and the Annual General Meeting. So, we thought that for complying with all the provisions of the Companies Act, as well a

items.statement: Geopolitical risk mitigated by advance payments and appreciating GPU assets; client concentration not seen as risk
items.quote: Actually -- yes, we actually focus on collecting maximum advance from the customer, and this is an appreciating asset. This is no longer a depreciating commodity. So, even if a customer who has paid you 15 months -18 months of advance, if that customer walks out, you have another customer ready to pay you a higher price and take over that customer.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR 133.66 crores, up 7.28% YoY; PAT INR 29.28 crores, up 14% YoY; EBITDA margin 42%
items.value: Revenue INR 133.66 cr, PAT INR 29.28 cr, EBITDA margin 42%
items.quote: Our revenue from operations came in at INR 133.66 crores, which has grown by 7.28% year-over-year, while our profit after tax has grown by 14%, reaching to INR 29.28 crores. Our EBITDA stood at INR 559 million, translating to a healthy margin of 42%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue down 20.2% QoQ due to one-time design services revenue in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Whereas, our total income stands at INR1,351.71 million in the current quarter, which is Q1 fiscal year '27, against which the corresponding number was INR1,257.21 million. And the total expenses of Q1 fiscal year '27 was INR987.04 million, whereas for the corresponding period last year was INR910.39 million.
